## Checking the proposed answer

**Exponent a.** Let σ = d/u + d/v and take u ≤ v. For a ball B of radius r and a point z in it, the Palm-type expected collision occupation of B is

∫ μ(B)·p¹ₛ(z,·)p²ₛ(z,·) ds ≍ r^d ∫_{r^u}^{1} s^{-σ} ds ≍ r^{u(1-d/v)}/(σ-1) = r^a/(σ-1),

with a = u(1 − d/v). The lower cutoff r^u is the larger of the two cutoffs r^u and r^v, since u ≤ v. Starting from a point at distance O(1), the expected collision occupation is ≍ r^d. So the probability that a ball meets the collision set is ≍ r^{d−a}, and the first-moment heuristic gives gauge r^a. The hypotheses d/v < 1 and σ > 1 are exactly the conditions under which this computation is dominated by the scale r^u. So the power a = u(1 − d/v) is well supported.

**Exponent c.** With a fixed, c = 1 − a/d = 1 − u/d + u/v. This has the same form as the Taylor–Pruitt exponent (1 − α/d) for the range of a single stable process, with α replaced by a. It is plausible, but I have not derived it.

**Exponent b.** The first-moment computation gives a pure power with no logarithm, because the integral ∫_{r^u}^1 s^{-σ} ds is dominated by its lower endpoint when σ > 1. Nothing in the heuristic produces a factor (log 1/r)^{σ−1}. The proposed b = d/u + d/v − 1 therefore has no support in the argument I could carry out. I also cannot rule out a log-power correction from a finer multi-scale or extreme-value effect, so I cannot confirm b.

**Conclusion.** The power a is verified and c is plausible by analogy. The logarithmic exponent b is the unverified piece, and the simplest heuristic points to b = 0. I am not certain that the proposed triple is wrong, but I would not accept it as correct without a reference or a sharper derivation of b.

VERDICT: REJECT
